**Second beta of the 0.4.7 line.** Still a pre-release: not marked Latest, not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use v0.4.6.

Linux x86_64 only — pre-releases ship the tarball. No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews.

beta.1 was the build we wanted flown for memory. This one fixes a startup crash found by a tester on that build, and clears the remaining reported defects.

---

## XEarthLayer could refuse to start, and the only fix was a file you had never heard of

A tester on beta.1 hit this:

```
┌ X-Plane Earth Layer 0.4.7-beta.1 ──────────────┐
│ Building Scenery Index...                      │
│ memory allocation of 3418906639127570548 bytes failed
│ Files indexed: 0                    Aborted (core dumped)
```

That number is not a quantity of memory. Written out in hexadecimal it is `0x2f726579616c6874`, which read as text is `thlayer/` — eight characters of the path `~/.xearthlayer/`. A damaged byte in the index cache had shifted every subsequent read along by one position, so a piece of a file path was read as a field saying how many bytes to allocate next. Nothing sane could satisfy it, and the process aborted before finishing startup.

The code already intended to handle this. It reads the cache, and if the read fails it throws the cache away and rebuilds from scratch. That is exactly right, and it had never once run: a failed allocation of that size terminates the process outright rather than reporting an error the surrounding code can catch. The recovery path was unreachable from the moment it was written.

**Every cache in XEarthLayer now bounds what it reads by the size of the file it is reading.** Nothing legitimate can need more bytes than the file contains, so a corrupt length is rejected instead of attempted. A cache that cannot be read is discarded and regenerated, which is what a cache is for. Caches are also written durably now, so an interrupted write cannot leave a half-finished file in place to be found later.

If you are on beta.1 and cannot start, this build fixes it. You do not need to delete anything.

## Upgrading from 0.4.6: expect one slower flight

**This affects you if your last stable build was 0.4.7-alpha or later — skip this section.** It applies to anyone coming from 0.4.6.

0.4.7-alpha.1 corrected how mipmaps are written into generated textures, which changed their size. Every texture cached by 0.4.6 is therefore the wrong size for this build. Until now those were detected at the last moment, replaced with a magenta placeholder, and — because nothing deleted them — served as magenta again on every subsequent request. Permanently, with no way back short of clearing the cache by hand.

They are now replaced properly the first time they are read. The cost is that your first flight after upgrading regenerates a large part of the texture cache: more downloading, more encoding, and more placeholder tiles than usual while it catches up. It settles after that.

## The placeholder timeout is now the documented 10 seconds

When a texture cannot be produced in time, XEarthLayer serves a magenta placeholder rather than making the simulator wait. That limit is `generation.timeout`, documented and reported as 10 seconds — but the setting never reached the code, which used a hardcoded 30. It is now honoured.

This is the right value and it is what the documentation has always claimed, but it is a real change: the window before a placeholder appears is three times shorter than the build you are running today. Combined with the cache refill above, the first flight after upgrading from 0.4.6 is where you are most likely to notice it. If you would rather have the old behaviour while the cache warms, set `timeout = 30` under `[generation]` and put it back afterwards.

## Also fixed

**The whole world could be marked as having no scenery.** Prefetch retires a region when it has no scenery to fetch there, so it stops asking. With no scenery index loaded, the check returned "nothing here" — which is indistinguishable from having looked and genuinely found nothing. Every region a flight touched was retired without anything having been consulted. If you fly without installed ortho packages, this is why the region counts looked the way they did. ([#228](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/228))

**`xearthlayer diagnostics` could hang forever.** Measuring the cache directory walked the entire tree; on a multi-terabyte cache it never finished, so the report never printed. Since the bug report form asks you to paste that output, this stopped people filing bugs at all. It is now bounded at five seconds and says so if it runs out of time. ([#251](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/251), reported by [@mmaechtel](https://github.com/mmaechtel))

**Two more settings that were being ignored.** `cache.dds_disk_ratio` never reached the cache, which always split its disk budget 60/40 no matter what you set — while the dashboard showed your figure, so the two disagreed. And `executor.max_concurrent_jobs` had moved to `[executor]` in an earlier release without the reader following, so a configuration file XEarthLayer had written itself could not be read back. ([#248](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/issues/248), reported by [@mmaechtel](https://github.com/mmaechtel))

---

## Reporting

`xearthlayer diagnostics` now completes, so please include it. The log at `~/.xearthlayer/xearthlayer.log` is overwritten on every launch — copy it aside before relaunching if you hit something worth reporting.

Most useful right now: whether the first flight after upgrading from 0.4.6 settles down as described, and roughly how long it takes to.
